A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-unification study. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–G support a complete comparison despite changed formatting and pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original DNA, protein, language, antibody-optimization, and MNIST experiments, plus simulations and numerical-stability analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and simulations, including the supplementary results in Appendices B, C, and G.

M1.justification: The Wright–Fisher construction, hollow and sufficient-statistic parameterizations, stable simplicial sampler, losses, and inference procedures are unchanged, including their appendix specifications.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FlyBrain DNA, UniRef50 protein, lm1b language, antibody-optimization, and MNIST coverage. No training or evaluation domain or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain DDSM, Dirichlet flow matching, and the individual versus unified diffusion models. The added acknowledgement of Benton et al. does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendices F–G retain the same splits, training budgets, architectures, metrics, and sampling procedures, including 48-hour protein training and language training on 33 billion tokens.

E4.justification: The Appendix B path simulations, Appendix C sampling-speed and numerical-stability analyses, and Appendix G antibody and MNIST analyses are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors in Figure 5, the Appendix B Mann–Whitney test using the same simulations, and 100 repeated antibody-optimization experiments. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run count changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, both report DNA ELBOs of 1.30 versus 8 nats per position, and Figures 7, 10, and 11 retain the same benchmark results.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, Proposition 6.1, the Appendix B counterexample, and the derivations and proofs in Appendices C–E are mathematically unchanged. Differences are citation and typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unification, likelihood and hyperparameter comparisons, stable simplicial diffusion, and competitive unified models.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries remain unchanged, including low-time numerical instability, large-vocabulary difficulties, the omitted diffusion frameworks, and the interpretation of MNIST results.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, training times, and code and data access information remain the same. URL wrapping and citation-format changes do not alter access or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5.2 newly acknowledges that Benton et al. proposed the same sampling procedure in a toy setting, and removes Richemond et al. from its SDE-sampling attribution. The conclusion adds citations for omitted frameworks, including a new Campbell et al. (2024) reference on discrete flows.

P1.justification: Numbered citations become author–year citations, and a few phrases and header elements change. The substantive prose, section order, and appendix organization remain largely identical.

P2.justification: The document adopts an ICLR conference template throughout, changing the title and affiliation layout, running headers, heading typography, spacing, and figure placement. Figures 10 and 11 now share a page, while Figure 6 moves relative to Figure 7. The underlying plots and images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the provenance of the Section 5.2 sampler clearer by explicitly acknowledging Benton's earlier use and adds supporting citations for omitted frameworks. This is a limited improvement in scholarly positioning; the methods, proofs, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
